correctness.rationale: The product of Bézout with adjunction is valid in every stated characteristic: off the exceptional curves and Q, -K·C≥d>0; for a negative curve, C²-(-K·C) is even and at least -2, forcing C²=-1, -K·C=1 and d=1. Thus the negative curves are exactly six exceptionals, fifteen pair-lines and Q. The anticanonical model identification also holds in characteristic two: if q is the conic equation, lift a cubic section of the conic with the six simple prescribed zeros to a plane cubic f. The anticanonical basis qx,qy,qz,f gives the cubic Wq(X,Y,Z)=f(X,Y,Z). Away from the projection vertex, smoothness follows where q≠0 by the W derivative and where q=0 by transversality of q=f=0. At the vertex the projective tangent conic q=0 is smooth. This is a single ordinary double point, resolved by the (-2)-conic. For the support count, the (-1)-curves must be mutually disjoint and the Schur complement for Q is -2+s, so at most one exceptional may accompany Q. The realization by big classes follows by correcting an ample A on the support via the positive-definite negative intersection matrix, whose off-diagonal entries are nonpositive; the corrected positive part is nef and big. Intersecting edge families on unused labels are singletons, stars, or a triangle, giving the stated split polynomial. Independent integral lattice congruence enumeration gives (1,22,156,490,725,447,57), Q profile (0,1,21,120,260,210,36), and totals 1898 and 648; the smooth comparison gives 2764 and hence difference 866. The negative index is six, so no seven-component support is possible. Enumeration verifies the lattice count; the geometric argument supplies position and characteristic independence.
residual_risks: No extrapolation to other singularity types, nonclosed-field arithmetic, or the singular surface's own divisor cone.
